03
Start here

The truth no one tells you.

  • 01 Retention is not just a revenue channel. Judged on attributed rupees alone, you see a quarter of it.
  • 02 It does not work in silos. WhatsApp alone, or email alone, leaves the money on the table.
  • 03 Half the outcome is outside our control: unit economics, product fit, landing pages, how acquisition spends.
  • 04 It is not a first-click channel, and usually not a last-click one either.
So why pay for it
Because it is four channels wearing one name, and only one of them shows up in the revenue report.
04
What it actually is

Four channels, one system.

Growth

Capture, recovery flows, launches and sales that bring people back.

Experience

Order journey, COD confirmation, activation. The utility layer that keeps a list warm cheaply.

Feedback

Quizzes, skin and fit profiles, preferences. The data that makes every later message specific.

Engagement

A real calendar. Stories, education, loyalty, community.

The whole job
Get the right message to the right person at the right time. Everything else is tooling.
05
How we work

Five stages. Most brands have built one and a half.

Stage 01

Acquisition

Capture, then a welcome that carries the offer all the way to the order.

Stage 02

Recovery

Browse, cart, checkout. Highest yield in Indian D2C, most commonly half built.

Stage 03

Activation

Post-purchase education, specific to what they bought.

Stage 04

Replenishment

Timed to your measured rebuy window, not a category guess.

Stage 05

Win-back

Usually the largest untouched asset on the account.

Operating rule

Campaign first, measure, then automate what performed. We do not build twenty flows on a theory.

Case study 01 · Fragrance · Uttar Pradesh

Built from nothing in 30 days.

₹4.8 Cr a month on Shopify. Retention was contributing under one percent of it.

Live retainer
0.68% → 4.07%Retention share of revenue
17.6% → 33.9%Returning share of orders
₹586 → ₹854AOV, up 46%
₹21K → ₹75KFlow revenue per month
What we did
  • Cohort calendar: lapsed, prospects, tester buyers, 2x, 3x, VIP. Each with its own mechanic.
  • Eleven flows built: checkout recovery, post-purchase, post-delivery, COD to prepaid, VIP 60-day.
  • Login popup rebuilt around a first-order gift that survives to checkout.
  • Founder-voice copy system with a locked guardrail list.
Key win
Checkout recovery earned ₹45,873 at 23x. The VIP-only Father's Day send below earned ₹91,791 at 9.42x, while the same offer to the cold list returned 1.1x. Same message, different people, nine times the return.

Three more, in brief

Same method, three categories.

Fashion

VIP community drove category expansion

83% of customers were stuck buying one category and launches were landing at a quarter of their potential. We built cross-category style journeys, a 1,800-member VIP WhatsApp circle with 48-hour early access and founder voice notes, and a five-touch pre-launch warm-up.

+26%Order frequency
3.5xLaunch performance
31%Repeat rate, 90 days
Skincare

Quiz to cash, ₹89 lakh

72% of customers never bought beyond the starter serum. We mapped the cross-sell sequence off 50,000 orders, ran a skin-type quiz that captured preferences on 40% of the list, and built eight lifecycle flows timed to when products actually run out.

+41%Cross-category rate
₹89 LRevenue, 7 months
1.8xFlow performance
Supplements

Community-led 48% retention

67% never reordered after the first bottle, because nobody was there after the sale. We built a 3,200-member WhatsApp wellness hub, bi-weekly expert AMAs, and replenishment timed to serving sizes rather than a calendar guess.

2.2xSubscription rate
48%90-day retention

Proof 01 · Email · Founder-led brands

Email revenue without a discount attached.

Two founder-led brands, Klaviyo, 2026. Sorted by revenue, not by opens.

Brand one · best send ₹4,27,862 from 37,627 recipients
Brand two · ₹43,598 from 9 orders, roughly ₹4,800 AOV
The two things worth noticing
On brand one the best send reached 37,627 people and made ₹4.27 lakh. Another reached 81,210 and made ₹69,035. Twice the list, a sixth of the money.

On brand two the click rates sit under 1% and the revenue still lands, because a founder-led email converts the handful of people who were ready. It does not chase clicks.

Proof 03 · Single sends · Cohort targeting

The same offer, priced by who receives it.

One fragrance brand, Father's Day 2026. The identical promotion sent to three different cohorts returned three different businesses.

Two-time-plus buyers only · ₹91,791 at 9.42 ROAS on ₹9,748 spend
Wider cohort · ₹58,590 at 5.21 ROAS on ₹11,243 spend
Third cohort, same offer
Sent to the cold list, the identical Father's Day promotion returned 1.1x. Nine times the return came from the targeting, not the creative and not the discount.

Proof 07 · Omnichannel distribution

Two brands. Opposite answers.

Where the retention revenue actually comes from, on two Indian accounts in the same year.

Brand one · WhatsApp 77%, email 23%
Brand two · SMS 54%, WhatsApp 40%, email 6%
Why we never quote a mix up front
Same country, same year, and the answer flips completely. Anyone who tells you the channel split before reading your data is selling you their template. We build the mix from your numbers, then keep moving it.
16
The audit

What we find when we open an account.

Six real accounts opened in 2026. Names withheld, numbers exact.

  • 01 Fitness, ₹300 Cr run rate. 12.66 lakh contacts in the panel, no email programme at all. Thirteen broadcasts ever.
  • 02 Acne skincare. An identity tool had recognised 43,306 shoppers in eight weeks. Messages sent: zero.
  • 03 Women's wellness. 3,43,579 emails in twelve months produced 824 clicks. Replenishment made 2 orders in 30 days.
  • 04 Checkout abandonment. ₹1.03 crore abandoned in one account, recovered at 0.2%. A second account: ₹68.9 lakh in one month at 0.47%.
  • 05 Premium skincare. The cheapest acquisition product brings the most customers and retains worst: 13% against 27.6%.
  • 06 Four accounts. WhatsApp delivery at 30 to 66% against 85 to 95% healthy, every failed send billed in full.
Browse flow pointed at a category nobody bought
₹1.03 Cr abandoned · 0.2% recovered · smart retry adding 33%

Category maths

The repeat window is not where you think.

Computed from each brand's own order export. This sets every replenishment delay, and it almost never does.

CategoryMedian days to 2nd orderLifetime repeatWhat it means
Acne skincare811.6%A day 20 delay misses 82% of buyers.
Barefoot footwear1017.2%Second pair inside a month, not a season.
Men's premium tees1020.2%76% of rebuys are the same tee in a new colour.
Women's wellness3023.3%Whole repeat business decided by day 56.
Premium skincare7419.7%A cross-sell window, not a replenishment one.
Why this is the first thing we compute
Four of these five were running one generic replenishment flow on a 30 or 45 day delay. On three, the money was already decided and lost before the message went out.

Engagement shape

The first 90 days.

Days 1 to 30

Foundation

  • Full audit on your own order data
  • Turn on capture
  • Build the recovery layer
  • Fix delivery before adding volume
Days 31 to 60

Acceleration

  • A real calendar, festivals and drops
  • Every cohort gets its own send
  • Win-back pointed at the lapsed pool
  • Copy in your voice, guardrails agreed up front
Days 61 to 90

Optimisation

  • Winners become flows
  • Activation and replenishment per product
  • Split tests on the two flows carrying the money
  • Reporting that leads with revenue share
